title: rootless container quadlet files do not  load anymore from ~/.config/containers/systemd  on Fedora 44
body:
### Issue Description

My rootless container do not start anymore on Fedora 44 Siilverblue.

SELinux is set to permissive.

XDG_CONFIG_HOME is empty.

I have podman-5.8.4-1.fc44.x86_64 installed.

pgsql.container:

```
[Unit]
Description=pgsql
After=local-fs.target

[Container]
Pod=pgsql.pod
Image=localhost/pgsql
Volume=pgsql:/var/lib/postgresql

[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target default.target
```
pgsql.pod

```
[Unit]
Description=pgsql
After=local-fs.target

[Pod]
PodName=pgsql
PublishPort=5432:5432

[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target default.target
```
I cannot start the container with systemd.

systemctl --user daemon-reload
systemctl --user start pgsql
Failed to start pgsql.service: Unit pgsql.service not found.

podman quadlet list

```
NAME             UNIT NAME          PATH ON DISK                                                  STATUS      APPLICATION
pgsql.container  pgsql.service      /var/home/fansari/.config/containers/systemd/pgsql.container  Not loaded
pgsql.pod        pgsql-pod.service  /var/home/fansari/.config/containers/systemd/pgsql.pod        Not loaded
```

### Steps to reproduce the issue

Steps to reproduce the issue
1. See above
2.
3.


### Describe the results you received

The podman container is not started becuase the service is not found.

### Describe the results you expected

The service should be found and the container should be started.

comments.body:
I found it works when I put my pgsql.container and pgsql.pod files here:

/etc/containers/systemd/users/60257

I can then create a symlink.

ln -s /etc/containers/systemd/users/60257 ~/.config/containers/systemd

It does not work the other way round (maybe because I use systemd-homedir).

It is not clear to me why ~/.config/containers/systemd suddenly stopped working.

quadlet can see the files there (podman quadlist list) but does not load them.

Everything worked until recently.
Hi! I'm interested in working on this issue.

> Hi! I'm interested in working on this issue.

Great. I also tried now to set XDG_CONFIG_HOME.

This environment variable is empty by default.

I tried to explicitely set it to either of these:

export XDG_CONFIG_HOME='/home/fansari/.config'

export XDG_CONFIG_HOME='/var/home/fansari/.config'

But nothing works. "podman quadlet list" finds the unit files but does not load them for some reason.

Putting them back to /etc/containers/systemd/users/60257 makes everything working again.

Was able to reproduce this on a fresh Fedora 44 Silverblue (aarch64) VM, and narrowed it down to `systemd-homed` specifically. Details below in case they help.

**Setup:** Fresh install via the official aarch64 OSTree ISO, kickstart-driven (`ostreecontainer --url=quay.io/fedora/fedora-silverblue:44`), podman 5.8.4 — same version as the original report. SELinux permissive.

**Attempt 1 — plain user account, did not reproduce.** Created a normal account the standard way (via kickstart's `user` command, i.e. the usual `useradd`-style path), placed the exact `pgsql.container`/`pgsql.pod` from this issue in `~/.config/containers/systemd/`, ran `systemctl --user daemon-reload` + `systemctl --user start pgsql`. This worked fine — `podman quadlet list` showed both units loaded and generated, and `systemctl --user start pgsql` actually invoked `podman run` (it only failed afterward because the `localhost/pgsql` test image doesn't exist here — unrelated). So the `/home → /var/home` symlink that's specific to ostree-based Fedora variants is **not** by itself the cause.

**Attempt 2 — `systemd-homed`-managed account, reproduced exactly.** Created a second account via `homectl create` instead:

```
sudo homectl create fansari --storage=directory --member-of=wheel --shell=/bin/bash -P
sudo loginctl enable-linger fansari
sudo homectl activate fansari
```

Worth noting: `homectl` allocated **UID 60257** — the exact UID shown in the original report's `podman info` idmap output. That's `systemd-homed`'s default UID range (60001+), not a coincidence, so it looks like the original reporter's account was in fact homed-managed ("maybe because I use systemd-homedir" in the thread above, probably referring to this).

Placing the identical quadlet files under this user's `~/.config/containers/systemd/` and running the exact same commands reproduced the issue precisely:

```
$ podman quadlet list
NAME             UNIT NAME          PATH ON DISK                                                  STATUS      APPLICATION
pgsql.container  pgsql.service      /var/home/fansari/.config/containers/systemd/pgsql.container  Not loaded
pgsql.pod        pgsql-pod.service  /var/home/fansari/.config/containers/systemd/pgsql.pod        Not loaded
$ systemctl --user start pgsql
Failed to start pgsql.service: Unit pgsql.service not found.
```

**Narrowing the cause:**

1. `fansari` had **no `/etc/subuid`/`/etc/subgid` entry at all** — `homectl create` doesn't allocate one, unlike Anaconda/`useradd`-based account creation. `podman quadlet list` even surfaces a warning about this (`no subuid ranges found for user "fansari"`). This looks like a real, separate provisioning gap for homed accounts — but manually adding a subuid/subgid range did **not** fix the quadlet loading problem, so it isn't the (sole) root cause here.
2. Running the generator directly (`/usr/libexec/podman/quadlet -dryrun -user`) as `fansari` works perfectly — it finds and parses both files and prints valid generated units, no errors. But after an actual `systemctl --user daemon-reload`, `/run/user/60257/systemd/generator.late/` contains no `pgsql*` units, and there's no journal trace of `quadlet-generator` running at all for that reload — while another user generator (`systemd-xdg-autostart-generator`) *does* produce output in the same directory for the same session. So generators are running in general; this one specifically isn't producing (or isn't being invoked) the same way it is under a manual shell.

That points at something in how systemd's user-manager invokes the quadlet generator for `systemd-homed` accounts specifically — plausibly an NSS/`systemd-userdbd` resolution gap at the point generators execute (i.e. the generator can't resolve the home/passwd entry for a homed user in that execution context the way it can for a normal account), causing it to silently find nothing rather than error. This looks related to systemd/systemd#29297 ("Rootless containers fail for homed-managed users"), though I haven't traced it to an exact line of code yet.

Happy to share the full kickstart/VM setup if useful for anyone else trying to reproduce.

subuid and subgid are there.

```
fansari@bat:~$ cat /etc/subuid                                                                                                                                                                                     
fansari:524288:65536
testuser:589824:65536

fansari@bat:~$ cat /etc/subgid
fansari:524288:65536
testuser:589824:65536
```
